questions.stem: In simple terms, what is a data lakehouse?
options: A data lake without any governance
Data warehouse + data lake, combining the strengths of both
A data warehouse hosted in the cloud
A NoSQL database for streaming
A virtual layer over operational systems
questions.explanation: The lakehouse is expressed simply as data warehouse plus data lake: the structured, governed nature of the warehouse combined with the flexible, large-scale storage of the lake.

questions.stem: Around when did the data lakehouse concept emerge?
options: Around 1990
Around 2000
Around 2010
Around 2020
Around 1975
questions.explanation: The data lakehouse emerged around 2020 as an architectural response to the limitations of both data warehouses and data lakes.

questions.stem: What long-standing weakness of traditional data lakes does the lakehouse address?
options: They could not store unstructured data
They lacked strong transactional guarantees, often leading to inconsistent or unreliable data sets
They were too expensive to scale
They could only run batch workloads
They required 3NF modelling
questions.explanation: Traditional lakes stored vast raw data but lacked strong transactional guarantees, while warehouses had consistency but struggled with semi-structured and unstructured data at scale.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the capabilities a data lakehouse offers?
options: ACID transactions
Upsert and delete operations
Schema-on-write support
Tight coupling of storage and compute
Batch and streaming compatibility
questions.explanation: The lakehouse decouples storage and compute; tight coupling was the limitation of earlier systems. ACID, upserts and deletes, schema-on-write and batch plus streaming are lakehouse capabilities.

questions.stem: What is the significance of open table formats such as Parquet in a data lakehouse?
options: They encrypt the data automatically
They make data natively accessible to analytical and data science tools
They restrict access to a single vendor's tools
They convert data into relational tables
They remove the need for metadata
questions.explanation: Open table formats such as Parquet make lakehouse data natively accessible to analytical and data science tools.

questions.stem: What architectural breakthrough of the lakehouse addresses the scalability bottlenecks of earlier systems?
options: Storing everything in memory
The decoupling of storage and compute, with compute clusters scaled independently
Replacing SQL with a new query language
Moving all data back into OLTP databases
Eliminating metadata management
questions.explanation: Earlier systems tightly coupled storage and compute; the lakehouse uses inexpensive, durable object storage as its foundation and scales compute clusters independently.

questions.stem: Which foundation does a data lakehouse use for storage?
options: Relational databases such as Oracle
Inexpensive, durable object storage such as Amazon S3, Azure Data Lake Storage or Google Cloud Storage
Tape archives
Local disks on each compute node
In-memory caches
questions.explanation: The lakehouse leverages inexpensive, durable object storage such as Amazon S3, Azure Data Lake Storage or Google Cloud Storage as its foundation.

questions.stem: Why is object storage alone not sufficient for a lakehouse, and what fills the gap?
options: It is too slow; the gap is filled by in-memory caching
It lacks reliability and governance; technologies such as Delta Lake add transactional integrity and metadata management on top
It cannot hold unstructured data; the gap is filled by HDFS
It is too expensive; the gap is filled by tape
It does not support Parquet; the gap is filled by CSV
questions.explanation: Object storage alone does not provide reliability and governance; Delta Lake and similar technologies add transactional integrity and metadata management, the tipping point that made the lakehouse practical.

questions.stem: How does schema-on-write support in a lakehouse compare with schema-on-read designs?
options: It allows weaker data contracts
It allows stronger data contracts
It removes the need for any schema
It only applies to unstructured data
It is identical to schema-on-read
questions.explanation: Schema-on-write support allows stronger data contracts than schema-on-read designs.

questions.stem: Why is the lakehouse model gaining momentum even though many organisations still maintain Hadoop-based data lakes?
options: Because it is free of charge
Because it unifies analytical, machine learning and streaming workloads in a single architecture, reducing overlapping silos and simplifying governance
Because it eliminates the need for object storage
Because it only supports structured data
Because regulators mandate it
questions.explanation: The lakehouse unifies analytical, machine learning and streaming workloads within one architecture, reduces overlapping silos and simplifies governance while balancing flexibility with reliability.
